headline_en: Lives ruined in the cycle of debt
summary_en: Prothom Alo looked at 24 indebted lower-middle-class families in five upazilas of Rajshahi (Bagha, Charghat, Paba, Mohanpur, Tanore) who took loans from several microcredit NGOs at once; some borrowed for family needs including sending a son abroad. Eight unnatural deaths of indebted people were reported in Rajshahi between 16 April and 23 September of the previous year. One farmer in Bagha took a 3 lakh taka loan partly to send his son abroad; the son fell into the hands of a broker ring and came back, and the father is now in hiding driving a rickshaw.

facts.statement: Of 24 indebted families Prothom Alo examined in Rajshahi's Bagha, Charghat, Paba, Mohanpur and Tanore upazilas (article published January 2026), every family had borrowed from several places at once; besides business and crop loans, some had borrowed for family needs such as a child's wedding, sending a son abroad and medical treatment.

Belayet Pramanik (40) of Majhpara Bausa village, Bagha upazila, Rajshahi, took a 3 lakh taka loan about 10 months before the report (published January 2026), used it to grow onions and to send his son abroad; the son fell into the hands of a broker ring (dalal chakra) and came back.

After his son's failed migration and losses on onions, Belayet Pramanik of Bagha, Rajshahi took loans from three more organisations, bringing his weekly instalments to 11,860 taka; unable to pay, he left home four or five months before the January 2026 report and now drives a rickshaw elsewhere, paying only what he can.

Between 16 April and 23 September of the year before the January 2026 report, eight unnatural deaths of indebted people, including four members of one family, were reported in Rajshahi; police and families said four were suicides, and one man killed his wife and two children and then himself.

Afzal Hossain, director of the Rajshahi NGO Rural Under Privileged and Landless Farmers Organisation (RULFAO), said microcredit NGO staff give 'target loans' to meet targets without feasibility checks and without checking how many other NGOs the borrower already owes.

Jahangir Alam, assistant director (HR and admin) of Shapla Gram Unnayan Sangstha, a Rajshahi lender, said that once the Credit Information Bureau (CIB) work is complete a borrower's ID card can be used to check whether they have loans at any other organisation or bank; he said young officers often lend in a hurry to meet targets and borrowers also hide information.
facts.source_in_article: Jahangir Alam, Shapla Gram Unnayan Sangstha

facts.statement: Bausa union parishad member Mohsin Ali said about 650 families live in Bausa village (Bagha, Rajshahi), of whom about 450 are burdened with debt, and 26 NGOs work in Bagha upazila.

Monira Khatun, deputy director of the Rajshahi district Department of Social Services, said no complaint had come that a borrower of an NGO registered with Social Services had committed suicide or fled home over debt, and that they could act if they received one.
facts.source_in_article: Monira Khatun, Department of Social Services, Rajshahi

headline_en: US visa bond is regrettable: Touhid Hossain
summary_en: Foreign adviser Md. Touhid Hossain called the US decision to add Bangladesh to a list of 38 countries whose citizens must post a visa bond of up to USD 15,000 regrettable but not unusual. The US State Department travel website announced the expansion on Tuesday (6 January 2026), adding 25 countries including Bangladesh. He said the government will seek an exemption through normal channels and repeated its stance against irregular migration, citing young men who go to Kenya on tourist visas.

facts.statement: The US State Department travel website announced on Tuesday (6 January 2026, per the 8 January report) that citizens of 38 countries, now including Bangladesh, must post a visa bond (security deposit) of up to USD 15,000 when applying to enter the United States.
facts.source_in_article: US State Department travel website, as reported

facts.statement: The US first put six countries on the visa bond list in August of the previous year (2025), then added seven more, and on Tuesday (6 January 2026) added 25 more including Bangladesh.

On 8 January 2026 foreign adviser Md. Touhid Hossain called the visa bond regrettable but not unusual, saying the list covers countries with immigration problems and that among people who take money from the US social system the number of Bangladeshis is high.
Asked whether the government would act against the visa bond, foreign adviser Touhid Hossain said it had just happened and Bangladesh would go through the usual process and try to get an exemption.

Foreign adviser Touhid Hossain said village youths go from Bangladesh to Kenya on tourist visas though they cannot actually afford to go to Kenya or Turkey, and that until this is stopped people will keep dying in the Mediterranean.

Touhid Hossain said the interim government has opposed irregular migration from its first day; someone who dies or is rescued crossing the Mediterranean is a victim deserving sympathy but has also broken the law.

Of a total planned spend of 8,43,26,427 taka, expatriate relatives and well-wishers will give 4,09,03,000 taka. headline_en: Returnee Hashem lost all savings to cancer, now earns lakhs from farming
summary_en: Abul Hashem (42) of Telibila village, Chorombo union, Lohagara, Chattogram went to Saudi Arabia in 2005 and ran two shops in Mecca. Diagnosed with stomach cancer in 2021, he wound up the business and returned, spending about 68 lakh taka on treatment. He now farms mixed winter vegetables on two acres bought with his earnings abroad, earning at least 3 lakh taka a year net, with advice, incentives and training from the upazila agriculture office.

facts.statement: Abul Hashem (42) of Telibila village, Chorombo union, Lohagara upazila, Chattogram, went to Saudi Arabia in 2005, owned two shops in Mecca which were his only income, and with that income bought two acres of land and built a brick house at home.

Abul Hashem was diagnosed with stomach cancer in 2021 and was forced to wind up his business in Mecca, Saudi Arabia and return to Bangladesh; his treatment has cost about 68 lakh taka so far, using all his savings, and still costs about 20,000 taka a month.

Lohagara upazila sub-assistant agriculture officer Rafiqul Kalam said returnee Abul Hashem receives regular technical advice, incentives and training from the agriculture office for his vegetable farming.
facts.source_in_article: Rafiqul Kalam, Lohagara upazila agriculture office

facts.statement: Returnee Abul Hashem earned at least 3 lakh taka net last year (2025) from mixed vegetables on his two acres in Lohagara, Chattogram, and his family expects about 4 lakh taka this year; he also runs a grocery shop, has started raising cattle and plans a supershop at the upazila centre.
facts.source_in_article: Abul Hashem's family, Prothom Alo reporter

headline_en: Hokkaido becoming the hub of decarbonisation projects and finance for Japan and Asia
summary_en: A press-tour report on Japan's green transformation (GX) push, with most of a planned 150 trillion yen investment going to Hokkaido and Sapporo in wind power, semiconductors, data centres and hydrogen. After a GX/finance conference in Sapporo in late November 2025, Sapporo's mayor announced decisions including a special visa for foreign engineers, which the reporter says could be an opportunity for Bangladeshi engineers. Sapporo's STEP office gives foreign companies free English-language help including visa advice, and subsidies are open to Bangladeshi entrepreneurs.

facts.statement: After the 'Global GX/Finance Summit Sapporo 2025' organised by Nikkei in Sapporo in the last week of November 2025, Sapporo mayor Katsuhiro Akimoto announced GX-finance decisions including relaxed regulations, subsidies and incentives, and the introduction of a special visa for foreign engineers; the reporter says this could be an attractive opportunity for Bangladeshi engineers. No visa details are given.
facts.source_in_article: Sapporo mayor Katsuhiro Akimoto, as reported by Prothom Alo correspondent

facts.statement: Kaori Nishiyama, director-general of Sapporo city's GX project, said about 40 trillion yen will be invested in GX (decarbonised infrastructure) business in Hokkaido over the next 10 years, in wind power, semiconductor production, data centres and a hydrogen-fuel transport system.
facts.source_in_article: Kaori Nishiyama, Sapporo city GX project

facts.statement: STEP (Sapporo Transnational Expansion and Partnership), a Sapporo city government body, gives foreign companies free help in English: links to local firms and Hokkaido University's Green Transformation Innovation Center, expert advice on administrative, customs and legal matters, networking events, visa advice, company set-up help and information on subsidies, per general manager Seiko Miura.

Sapporo offers companies tax exemptions for up to 10 years and subsidies: up to 200 million yen for head-office rent, up to 100 million yen rent for IT, content and biotech firms, up to 1 billion yen for factories, logistics and R&D sites, and up to 500,000 yen for start-ups' initial inspection visits; the report says entrepreneurs from Bangladesh and Bangladeshis living in Japan can use these.

Startup Hokkaido, set up in 2023 by Sapporo city, Hokkaido prefecture and the Hokkaido Bureau of Economy, Trade and Industry, will hold a global start-up conference called 'SHAKE-H' (শেইক-এইচ) in Sapporo from 22 to 26 February; its focus areas are agriculture and food, space, and environment and energy.
facts.source_in_article: Kiyohei Fujima, Startup Hokkaido executive director

headline_en: 9 million people in the UK, including those of Bangladeshi, Pakistani and Indian origin, could lose citizenship
summary_en: A report published by UK groups Runnymede Trust and Reprieve on Thursday (11 December 2025) says about 9 million people, about 13% of the UK population, could legally be stripped of British citizenship by the home secretary. Under current law citizenship can be removed if the government thinks a person is eligible for another country's citizenship, even if they never lived there. People with ties to Pakistan, Bangladesh, Somalia, Nigeria, North Africa and the Middle East are most at risk.

facts.statement: Under current UK law a British citizen's citizenship can be revoked if the government believes they are eligible for another country's citizenship, even if they have never lived in that country or do not consider themselves its citizen, according to a Runnymede Trust and Reprieve report published in December 2025.

The Runnymede Trust and Reprieve report (published Thursday, about 11 December 2025) says about 9 million people in the UK, about 13% of the population, could legally lose citizenship under the home secretary's power; those with links to Pakistan, Bangladesh, Somalia, Nigeria, North Africa and the Middle East are most at risk.

Per the Reprieve and Runnymede analysis, three in five people from non-white groups are at risk of losing British citizenship against one in 20 white Britons, a 12 times higher risk; about 984,000 people of Indian origin, 679,000 of Pakistani origin and 3.3 million Asian Britons including Bangladeshis are among the most potentially affected.

The best-known UK citizenship-revocation case is Shamima Begum, UK-born, whose citizenship was revoked on the claim that she was a Bangladeshi citizen, which the Bangladesh government denied; she had left the UK as a teenager to join IS and the UK rejected her application to return.

The report came as Conservative and Reform UK politicians talk of plans that could remove hundreds of thousands of people legally living in the UK; the UK Home Office had not commented at the time of writing.

headline_en: UK penalty for visa fraud: 10-year travel ban
summary_en: British High Commissioner in Dhaka Sarah Cooke said in a statement on 25 November 2025 that anyone from Bangladesh who uses visa fraud or illegal routes to go to the UK will be given a 10-year travel ban. The statement warned that criminal networks promise guaranteed visas, jobs without qualifications or fast processing for extra fees, and that victims instead suffer financial loss, refusals, bans and sometimes trafficking.

facts.statement: British High Commissioner in Dhaka Sarah Cooke said in a statement from the UK High Commission on Tuesday 25 November 2025 that anyone who uses visa fraud or an illegal route to go from Bangladesh to the UK will be given a 10-year travel ban by the UK government, as part of its fight against fake visas.
facts.source_in_article: British High Commission Dhaka statement, Sarah Cooke

facts.statement: High Commissioner Sarah Cooke said the UK welcomes only legitimate visa applications made through official channels and the correct route; those who attempt fraud face serious consequences including a 10-year travel ban.

The UK High Commission statement said criminal gangs use increasingly sophisticated methods to cheat prospective visa applicants, often promising guaranteed visas for extra fees, jobs without proper qualifications, or fast processing; in reality victims face financial loss, visa refusal, travel bans and, in the worst cases, trafficking and exploitation.

The UK High Commission statement said fraudulent activity by criminals and fraudsters causes losses of millions of pounds every year and puts vulnerable people worldwide, including in Bangladesh, at risk of exploitation, financial loss and legal consequences.

headline_en: Fellowship in America: apply with English proficiency
summary_en: Applications are open for the fully funded Fulbright Visiting Scholar Program 2026-27 in the US, for Bangladeshi professionals, university teachers and researchers with 10 or more years of experience to do research or teach for one academic year. Candidates need a PhD or equivalent professional degree and English proficiency; the programme starts next September. The deadline is stated as 20 December 2026, 11:59 am Bangladesh time.

facts.statement: The US Fulbright Visiting Scholar Program 2026-27, announced on the US Embassy Dhaka Facebook page (reported November 2025), gives fully funded grants for one academic year of research or teaching at a US institution to experienced Bangladeshi government and private professionals, university teachers, and researchers at research institutions with 10 or more years of professional experience.

Fulbright Visiting Scholar applicants must hold a PhD or equivalent professional degree, submit a research and teaching proposal in their field, and have English proficiency for professional work at a US university; the exchange starts in September of next year (2026 per November 2025 article).

Fulbright Visiting Scholar 2026-27 proposals are invited in all education-related fields, with priority to university administration and curriculum, distance learning, education technology, public health, biology, pharmacy, climate change and disaster management, urban planning and international relations; some short-term grants are also given for needs assessment, faculty development exchanges and curriculum or material design.

Fulbright Visiting Scholar benefits include return airfare, teaching and related academic fees, a monthly stipend for room, lodging and incidentals, a book allowance, health and accident insurance, and travel and excess baggage allowances.

To apply for the Fulbright Visiting Scholar Program, create a login account on the online application form; full instructions and application details are at https://bd.usembassy.gov/call-for-applications-for-the-2026-27-fulbright-visiting-scholar-program/.
For more information on the Fulbright Visiting Scholar Program, contact dhakausexchanges@state.gov.

The article gives the Fulbright Visiting Scholar 2026-27 application deadline as 'next year 20 December, 2026', by 11:59 am Bangladesh time (as printed in a November 2025 article; the year may be an error).

Over the past 50 years about 200-plus Bangladeshis have taken part in the Fulbright Visiting Scholar exchange, including academics, researchers, senior government officials and development professionals.

headline_en: How to get a work visa in Australia after finishing studies
summary_en: An explainer on Australia's Temporary Graduate visa, which lets international students who complete a degree in Australia stay two to three years to work, study further or travel, depending on the degree. It lists eligibility conditions, durations by degree and a base application fee of AUD 2,300. Indian students get extra duration under the AI-ECTA trade agreement; the article says students of other countries also get the visa.

facts.statement: Australia's Temporary Graduate visa lets international students who complete higher education in Australia stay for a set time to work, study further or travel; holders can live and work two to three years depending on the degree, but it does not guarantee a job and they must find work themselves.

Temporary Graduate visa durations in Australia: bachelor's (including honours) two years; master's (coursework or extended) two years; master's (research) three years; doctoral (PhD) three years; graduate diploma holders usually two years, which may vary with personal circumstances.

To apply for Australia's Temporary Graduate visa the applicant must hold a valid student visa and have completed a degree from an approved Australian institution, meet health and character requirements, hold adequate health insurance, and repay any debts to the Australian government; family members can be included in the same application or apply separately later.

The base application fee for Australia's Temporary Graduate visa is AUD 2,300, with possible extra costs for health examination, police certificate and biometrics; processing time varies with completeness of the application and document checks.

Indian students get additional, longer Temporary Graduate visa periods under the Australia-India Economic Cooperation and Trade Agreement (AI-ECTA); the article says students from other countries also get this work visa opportunity.

headline_en: Couple arrested over alleged swindling of 4.5 crore taka
summary_en: RAB-6 arrested a Madaripur couple, Zahirul Islam (40) and Nur Nahar (34) of Ishibpur village, Rajoir, at the Benapole border area in Jashore on Saturday 15 November 2025 over allegations of taking about 4.36 crore taka from people by promising to send them abroad and business deals. Both were already convicted in fraud cases and had been hiding while posing as Canada expatriates using Canadian phone numbers. A lawyer victim said they took 22 lakh taka to send him to Australia.

facts.statement: RAB-6 arrested Zahirul Islam (40) and his wife Nur Nahar (34) of Ishibpur village, Rajoir upazila, Madaripur, at the Benapole border area of Jashore on Saturday 15 November 2025, accused of taking 4 crore 36 lakh taka from various people by promising to send them abroad and business deals; on 16 November the Madaripur court sent them to jail.
facts.source_in_article: police, RAB, Rajoir police OC Mohammad Masud Khan

facts.statement: Zahirul Islam was sentenced to one year in a fraud case at a Madaripur court in 2023 and Nur Nahar to six months in a fraud case in 2024, but both had been in hiding.
The Madaripur couple Zahirul Islam and Nur Nahar hid inside Bangladesh while presenting themselves as Canada expatriates and contacting people using Canadian phone numbers.

Victims said Nur Nahar had been an NGO worker who built close relationships with many people while going door to door giving loans and collecting money, then took money from them with false stories and fled with her husband.

Lawyer Emon Hossain said the Madaripur couple took 22 lakh taka from him promising to send him to Australia, later gave him a cheque for 21 lakh taka, and his case on that cheque led to their arrest with help from RAB-6 and the Rajoir police OC.

headline_en: How many mobile phones can returning travellers bring duty-free
summary_en: Under Bangladesh's Baggage Rules for non-tourists, a passenger returning from abroad can bring one new mobile phone duty-free plus two used phones. More new phones are subject to duty and tax, up to 25,000 taka per phone.

facts.statement: Under Bangladesh's Baggage Rules for non-tourists (অপর্যটক ব্যাগেজ রুলস), a passenger returning from abroad can bring one new mobile phone duty-free, plus two used phones of their own.

headline_en: Canada's new immigration plan: chance for temporary residents to become permanent
summary_en: Canada's 2025 federal budget, tabled on 4 November 2025 by Prime Minister Mark Carney's Liberal minority government, plans to give permanent residence to up to 33,000 temporary work-permit holders in 2026 and 2027. The 2026 temporary resident intake target is cut to 385,000 (about 43% below 673,650 in 2025), with international students cut to 155,000 and temporary foreign workers to 230,000. The permanent resident target for 2026 stays at 380,000.

facts.statement: Canada's 2025 federal budget, presented to parliament on 4 November 2025 by Prime Minister Mark Carney's Liberal minority government, plans to grant permanent residence (PR) to up to 33,000 foreign workers holding temporary work permits in 2026 and 2027.

Canada's 2026 target for admitting temporary residents is 385,000, about 43% lower than 673,650 in 2025; within it, international students are cut almost by half to 155,000 and temporary foreign workers by 37% to 230,000.
Canada's 2026 permanent resident target stays at 380,000, 64% in economic immigration: 239,800 economic class, 84,000 family reunification and 56,200 refugee and humanitarian.
The Canadian government said its plan will give special priority to rural and remote regions hurt by labour shortages and tariff changes.

Prime Minister Mark Carney said in September 2025 that the Temporary Foreign Worker Program (TFWP) must be restructured to match real labour demand in specific sectors and regions; the 2025 budget gives no separate figure, but more work permits are expected to be issued under the International Mobility Program.

From January to August 2025 only 42% of the targeted temporary foreign workers and 29% of the targeted international students arrived in Canada, so the government says the lower targets do not mean a sudden stop to entries.

headline_en: BSF returns 19 Bangladeshis through Chauddagram border
summary_en: India's Border Security Force (BSF) handed 19 Bangladeshis (9 women, 9 men, 1 child) to Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) at a flag meeting at Amanganda, Chauddagram, Cumilla on 30 October 2025. They had gone to India illegally at various times and been held by Indian police and BSF, many serving jail terms. BGB handed them to Chauddagram police, filed a case against them, and they were to be sent to court in Cumilla the next day.

facts.statement: On Thursday 30 October 2025 India's BSF handed over 19 Bangladeshis (9 women, 9 men and 1 child) to BGB through a flag meeting near border pillar 2104 at Amanganda, Chauddagram upazila, Cumilla; the BSF team was led by Dipankar Saha, commander of Dakshin Bhabanipur Newnidia BSF camp, Tripura, and the BGB team by Md. Mostafa, commander of Amanganda BOP.
facts.source_in_article: Lt Col Mir Ali Ejaz, commander 10 BGB Cumilla; Cumilla BGB

facts.statement: Amanganda BOP commander Md. Mostafa said the 19 returned Bangladeshis had gone to India by illegal routes at different times and been caught by Indian police and BSF; many served sentences in various Indian jails.

Lt Col Mir Ali Ejaz said BGB told BSF not to push anyone in illegally and to inform BGB of any illegal Bangladeshis they hold; BSF sent the 19 people's names and identities, BGB verified through various means that all were Bangladeshi citizens, and then the handover took place by flag meeting.
facts.source_in_article: Lt Col Mir Ali Ejaz, 10 BGB

facts.statement: Chauddagram police OC Mohammad Helal Uddin Ahmed said BGB handed the 19 returnees to the police station and filed a case against them; they are from Bagerhat, Khulna and the northern region and were to be sent to court in Cumilla on Friday 31 October 2025.

headline_en: MACES: a bridge to a global future for Bangladeshi students
summary_en: A promotional profile of MACES, a Bangladeshi study-abroad consultancy founded in 2007 that says it represents over 200 universities in the UK, US, Canada, Australia, Japan and Malaysia. It claims credit for UK universities accepting Bangladeshi private-university bachelor's degrees for direct master's entry, credit-transfer routes, and introducing English-medium Japanese universities. It gives branch locations, opening days, website and phone number.

facts.statement: MACES, a study-abroad consultancy that began in 2007 as representative of one university, says it is now an authorised representative of over 200 universities in the UK, US, Canada, Australia, Japan and Malaysia; its founder Tina Salem Manzoor and managing partner Ruham Manzoor are described as British Council and British High Commission trained education consultants (promotional article).

The article says that before 2011-12 many UK universities required Bangladeshi applicants to have an extra master's degree, and that bachelor's degrees from Bangladeshi private universities are now accepted directly for UK master's programmes (credited to MACES's initiative).
The article says Bangladeshi business students in their second or third year can complete equivalent courses and enter the final year directly in the UK to earn a UK degree (credit transfer).
The article says MACES first introduced English-medium Japanese universities to Bangladeshi students and that since 2011 thousands of students have gone to study in Japan with scholarships.

MACES runs an annual 'MACES Education Meet' since 2017 in Dhaka, Chattogram, Sylhet, Khulna and Rangpur where students meet representatives of universities from the UK, US, Australia, Japan, Malaysia and Canada.
MACES branches in Dhaka (Gulshan and Dhanmondi), Sylhet and Chattogram give in-person advice six days a week, Saturday to Thursday; appointments at www.macesbd.com, phone 01755660012.

named_actors.name: MACES
named_actors.what_the_article_says: Study-abroad consultancy founded 2007; claims to represent 200+ universities and high visa success rate (promotional article).

headline_en: Japanese entrepreneur to set up driving school in Bangladesh to recruit drivers for Japan
summary_en: Miki Watanabe, founder of Japan's Watami Group, told Chief Adviser Muhammad Yunus in Dhaka on Saturday (25 October 2025) that he plans a driving school in Bangladesh to train large numbers of drivers for jobs in Japan, and is looking for a 12,000 square metre site. Watanabe already runs a language training academy in Monohardi, Narsingdi that plans to train and place at least 3,000 Bangladeshis; 52 workers have already gone to Japan for construction and agriculture. Yunus asked for more Japanese language test sittings, currently only twice a year.

facts.statement: Miki Watanabe, Japanese entrepreneur and politician and founder of Watami Group, announced at a meeting with Chief Adviser Muhammad Yunus at state guest house Jamuna, Dhaka, on Saturday (25 October 2025) a plan to set up a driving school in Bangladesh to recruit large numbers of trained drivers for jobs in Japan; he said they are looking for a 12,000 square metre site and that demand for skilled drivers in Japan is very high.

Chief Adviser Muhammad Yunus immediately instructed officials to identify suitable land on the outskirts of Dhaka for Watami Group's driving school, and expressed interest in another training centre in or near Dhaka so Japanese companies need not travel to Monohardi, Narsingdi.
During Chief Adviser Yunus's visit to Japan in May 2025, Japanese entrepreneurs signed an agreement to recruit 100,000 workers from Bangladesh over the next five years.

Watami Group founder Miki Watanabe has set up a language training academy in Monohardi, Narsingdi district, planning to train and recruit at least 3,000 Bangladeshis; batches currently have 40 students each and will be scaled up gradually.
Miki Watanabe said 52 workers trained through his Monohardi, Narsingdi academy have already gone to Japan to work in construction and agriculture.
Chief Adviser Yunus called for more Japanese language proficiency test sittings in Bangladesh, saying the test is currently held only twice a year, which is not enough for growing demand.

Yunus said teaching Japanese culture, etiquette and behaviour should be an essential part of training so Bangladeshis understand Japan and are properly prepared before going; he urged Watami Group to expand training in service, nursing, construction and agriculture, where skilled workers can earn well in Japan, and Watanabe said they want to do this too.
facts.source_in_article: Chief Adviser Muhammad Yunus, Miki Watanabe

facts.statement: The Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment has a newly formed Japan Cell that facilitates cooperation between Japanese investors and Bangladeshi institutions, praised by the Chief Adviser.

named_actors.name: Miki Watanabe / Watami Group
named_actors.what_the_article_says: Founder of Watami Group; runs a language academy in Monohardi that has sent 52 workers to Japan; plans a driving school in Bangladesh to recruit drivers for Japan.

headline_en: Bangladesh and Kuwait agree to strengthen ties in politics, economy and defence
summary_en: At the first Bangladesh-Kuwait foreign-secretary-level political consultations in Dhaka on Sunday 19 October 2025, the two countries agreed to deepen cooperation including on labour and employment of Bangladeshi workers. Kuwait's assistant foreign minister Samih Essa Johar Hayat said a new agreement renewing labour cooperation is being prepared, likely to be signed during a future high-level visit, and both sides reviewed expanding manpower cooperation in line with Kuwait Vision 2035. He gave current weekly flight numbers and said more routes and flights were agreed.

facts.statement: Kuwait's assistant foreign minister for Asian affairs Samih Essa Johar Hayat said after the first Bangladesh-Kuwait political consultations in Dhaka on Sunday 19 October 2025 that preparations are under way to sign a new agreement renewing labour cooperation, likely to be completed during a future high-level visit.
facts.source_in_article: Samih Essa Johar Hayat, Kuwait assistant foreign minister

facts.statement: The Bangladesh-Kuwait joint statement of 19 October 2025 said both sides reviewed expanding manpower cooperation in line with 'Kuwait Vision 2035' and finalising memoranda of understanding under discussion; employment of Bangladeshi workers was among the priority topics, and several new agreements are to be signed soon.
facts.source_in_article: Bangladesh-Kuwait joint statement; Samih Essa Johar Hayat

facts.statement: Kuwait's assistant foreign minister said that, as of October 2025, Kuwait Airways operates 7 flights a week, Jazeera Airways 14 and Biman Bangladesh Airlines 3 between the two countries, and that the sides agreed to add new routes and flights to Bangladesh soon.

Bangladesh and Kuwait agreed to hold political consultations every two years, alternating between Dhaka and Kuwait City, to revive the joint trade committee and hold a Bangladesh-Kuwait business forum in 2026; Bangladesh was represented by foreign secretary (bilateral) Nazrul Islam.

headline_en: Unable to go abroad, Kishoreganj youth rents a loudspeaker to hurl abuse
summary_en: Sarowar Hossain Rabbi (27) of Dakshin Panan village, Gobindapur union, Hossainpur, Kishoreganj rented a loudspeaker to abuse local people he blamed for blocking his loan applications, and posted the video on Facebook on Friday (17 October 2025). He said he had been unable to go to Saudi Arabia for three or four months for lack of 1 lakh taka, that his visa and medical would expire on 30 October, and that his visa had already expired twice before.

facts.statement: Sarowar Hossain Rabbi (27) of Dakshin Panan village, Gobindapur union, Hossainpur upazila, Kishoreganj said in a Facebook video (posted Friday 17 October 2025) that for three or four months he had been unable to go to Saudi Arabia because he lacked 1 lakh taka, and had applied to various samitis (lending associations) for a loan.
facts.source_in_article: Sarowar Hossain Rabbi, in his video

facts.statement: Sarowar Hossain Rabbi showed a visa paper in his video and said his Saudi visa and medical would expire on 30 October 2025, and that his visa had already expired twice before.

Sarowar Hossain Rabbi alleged that some local people spoke badly of him to lending samitis so he would not get a loan to go to Saudi Arabia; he tried and failed to raise the money by driving an auto-rickshaw and through a bKash partnership business, and rented a loudspeaker to abuse them in anger, later apologising in the video caption.

people_cases.what_happened: Could not get a loan from samitis, allegedly because locals spoke against him; visa expired twice already, current visa and medical expiring 30 October 2025
people_cases.outcome: Rented a loudspeaker to abuse locals and posted video; still unable to go

headline_en: Bodies of seven Sandwip expatriates killed in Oman return home
summary_en: The bodies of seven migrants from Sandwip, Chattogram, who worked catching fish at sea in Oman and died in a head-on road crash at Sidra in Oman's Duqm area on 8 October 2025, arrived at Chattogram's Shah Amanat International Airport on a Biman flight on Saturday 18 October 2025. The airport authority handed them to relatives at 9:20 pm, and the upazila administration arranged a joint janaza at East Sandwip High School ground the next morning.

facts.statement: Seven Bangladeshi migrants from Sandwip, Chattogram, who worked catching fish at sea in Oman, died on 8 October 2025 when the vehicle carrying them collided head-on with another vehicle in the Sidra area of Duqm (ধুকুম) province, Oman: Amin Majhi (50), Md. Sahabuddin (28), Md. Bablu (28), Md. Rocky (27), Md. Arju (26), Md. Jewel (28) and Mosharraf Hossain Rony (26).

The bodies of the seven Sandwip migrants killed in Oman arrived on a Biman Bangladesh flight at Shah Amanat International Airport, Chattogram, at 8:15 pm on Saturday 18 October 2025, ten days after the crash, and the airport authority handed them to relatives at 9:20 pm.
facts.source_in_article: Prothom Alo report; Ali Azgar, brother of Amin Majhi

facts.statement: The Sandwip upazila administration arranged a joint janaza for the seven migrants killed in Oman at 9:15 am on Sunday 19 October 2025 at East Sandwip High School ground near Enam Nahar Mor, per upazila nirbahi officer Mongchingnu Marma.

people_cases.who: Amin Majhi (50), Md. Sahabuddin (28), Md. Bablu (28), Md. Rocky (27), Md. Arju (26), Md. Jewel (28), Mosharraf Hossain Rony (26), all of Sandwip, Chattogram
people_cases.what_happened: Fishing workers killed in a head-on road crash in Sidra, Duqm, Oman on 8 October 2025
people_cases.outcome: Bodies returned to Chattogram airport on 18 October 2025; joint janaza in Sandwip
